biography.plain_text: Jonas Lindroth is a Swedish software entrepreneur and co-founder of international calling company Rebtel. Earlier, he worked in consultancy and technical support before becoming a part-owner of Sendit, the mobile internet software business acquired by Microsoft. He subsequently held his Rebtel investment through his own companies, HighWave Consulting and WindWave.

long_biography.plain_text:
Software entrepreneur Jonas Lindroth helped devise a system that used text messages to notify mobile users when new email arrived. Working with a team whose patent was assigned to Microsoft, he contributed to a method that attached an identifier to the alert. The phone could then request the corresponding email from its server.

In a separate invention with Hjalmar Winbladh, Lindroth tackled the allocation of telephone numbers for international calls. Their system combined the caller's identity with a local access number to identify the intended recipient. This allowed a limited pool of numbers to serve many customers, without requiring each person to install special software.
